changelog: Cause confirmed: a freshly-created (or resumed) backtest session fetched candles ending exactly at its own replay cursor with no explicit lead-in, so a session starting at (or near) the earliest available candle for its symbol/timeframe received only that one bar. Lightweight Charts' price scale and fitContent() both autoscale to whatever's actually loaded, so a single bar's own high/low filled the entire vertical axis and its one time-slot filled the entire horizontal one -- the reported giant candle block. This became far more visible after v3.20.6, which now defaults/prefills Start Date to the earliest available date on every symbol/timeframe change -- the overwhelmingly common case is now exactly the zero-lead-in edge case.

Fix: btLoadCandleWindow() (js/backtest.js) now explicitly requests BT_LEAD_IN_BARS (300, a named constant) candles before the replay point plus the current one, on every fresh load of the replay window -- session open, session resume, and after every advance, since it's one shared function rather than a create-only special case. get_backtest_candles' own no-lookahead clamp (BacktestController::getCandles()'s cursorCeiling) is completely unchanged -- this only changes how much history is requested, never what's allowed after the replay point, on any timeframe.

Fix: the replay window now sets a fixed-width initial visible range (the most recent BT_INITIAL_VISIBLE_BARS = 100 bars ending at the replay point) instead of calling fitContent(), which is what actually produced the giant-block look. Requested even when fewer than 100 real bars exist -- Lightweight Charts renders the real bars at a normal width with empty space filling the rest, rather than stretching sparse data to fill the pane. If a session's start date has fewer than 300 candles behind it, the server already returns however many actually exist with no error; the frontend already handled a shorter-than-requested result correctly (same pattern chart.js's own pagination already used).

Confirmed, no code change needed: scrolling back to load older history already works in the replay window -- chart.js's existing scroll-triggered loadOlderCandles() is symbol/timeframe-agnostic and already routes through window.btFetchCandlesOverride during an active session, unchanged by this release.

Finding, not a code change: there is currently no live control to switch timeframe during an active replay (no .tf-btn or equivalent exists in the replay window's controls bar) -- chart.js's onChartTimeframeChange()/loadInitialWindow() are the plain-browsing page's own mechanism and are not wired into the Backtesting page at all. If this is added later, it must call the lead-in-aware btLoadCandleWindow() (or route through it), not chart.js's own generic loadInitialWindow(), to inherit this fix automatically.
release_notes: No new migration in this release. Nothing was deployed or migrated as part of this turn, per instruction.
